task_signatures.correct_strategy: Replace entire patch with Gly-Ser linker (e.g. GSGG/GSGSG) to eliminate charge and PTM sites while preserving backbone flexibility and segment length
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Individual conservative swaps (E→Q, D→N, S→A) that neutralize charge but may partially rigidify the IDR or leave phosphorylation context intact

task_signatures.correct_strategy: S/T → A for the PTM-accepting residue; extend to flanking acidic residues only if they form a composite docking surface with evidence
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Replacing all nearby E/D residues without evidence they contribute to the kinase docking site

task_signatures.correct_strategy: C → A for buried cysteines; C → S for surface-exposed cysteines where retaining a hydroxyl is more conservative
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: C → G introduces excessive flexibility and may destabilize local structure

task_signatures.correct_strategy: Ala-scan strictly the identified contact residues; preserve all non-contact positions to avoid confounding structural effects
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Mutating entire surface patch including residues not in the contact map

task_signatures.correct_strategy: Confirm burial status first; buried hydrophobic → Ala; surface-exposed hydrophobic → Ser may be preferred to avoid aggregation
task_signatures.wrong_strategy: Applying the same substitution regardless of burial depth

failure_modes: context_blind_charge_neutralization: treating IDR the same as ordered domain, choosing E→Q/D→N without considering disorder propensity
phospho_site_only: blocking S phosphorylation but ignoring flanking acidic residues that together form the inhibitory patch
ignoring_function_as_unit_clue: when the question states residues act together, individual swaps are weaker than a unified patch replacement
over_engineering_disordered_region: introducing structured or bulky residues that collapse IDR flexibility
length_altering_substitution: inserting or deleting residues when only substitution is appropriate
key_principles: Always determine region type (IDR vs ordered domain vs linker) before choosing substitution strategy
For IDR/linker: prefer whole-patch Gly-Ser replacement over individual conservative swaps
Gly and Ser have high disorder propensity; Ala has moderate beta-propensity and can nucleate structure in long runs — avoid poly-Ala in IDR contexts
Substitution should preserve residue count (no insertions/deletions unless asked)
Minimize perturbation: only mutate residues within the identified functional patch
